name: FlightAware
summary: Flight tracking with detailed route history and delay analytics.
detail: Comprehensive flight tracking covering commercial and some general aviation. Strong on historical flight data — view all flights for a specific tail number going back years. Also tracks delays, cancel…
howTo: Search by flight number or aircraft registration (N-number)
View the 'Flight History' tab for historical records

name: Planespotters.net
summary: Aircraft photo database with fleet and registration records.
detail: Photo database combined with fleet data. Look up any aircraft registration to see its photo history, airline history, and current status. Useful for confirming an aircraft's identity and history.
howTo: Search by registration (N-number or country equivalent)
Review the aircraft's full history: previous operators, repaintings

name: Icarus Flights
summary: Track private jet tail numbers with flight history.
detail: Specifically focused on private jet tracking. Enter a tail number for a comprehensive history of its flights. Useful for tracking the movements of corporate jets and high-net-worth individuals.
howTo: Enter the aircraft tail number
Review the flight history map and timeline

name: MarineTraffic
summary: The leading real-time AIS ship tracking platform.
detail: Tracks 200,000+ vessels worldwide using AIS (Automatic Identification System) transponder data. View real-time position, vessel details, voyage history, and port calls. Essential for maritime intellig…
howTo: Search by vessel name, MMSI number, or IMO number
View current position and speed on the map
proTip: AIS can be spoofed or disabled. For sensitive targets, cross-reference with satellite imagery and port call records.

name: VesselFinder
summary: Alternative AIS ship tracker with photo database.
detail: Real-time vessel tracking with a large photo database of ships. Good alternative to MarineTraffic. The photo database helps visually confirm a vessel's identity.
howTo: Search by vessel name, MMSI, or IMO
View on the map or in list view

name: Maritime Awareness Project
summary: NBR's tool for tracking vessel movements in contested regions.
detail: The National Bureau of Asian Research's maritime tracking tool focused on the Indo-Pacific region. Tracks vessels in contested waters and overlays with exclusive economic zone boundaries.
howTo: Browse the map of the Indo-Pacific region
Filter by vessel type and time period

name: ICC Live Piracy Map
summary: Real-time map of reported piracy and armed robbery incidents at sea.
detail: The International Maritime Bureau's live piracy reporting map. Shows current piracy incidents, attacks, and suspicious approaches. Updated in near real-time from vessel reports.
howTo: Browse the interactive map
Click incident markers for report details

name: Google Hacking Database (GHDB)
summary: Community database of 8000+ Google dorks for finding exposed data.
detail: The Exploit-DB Google Hacking Database is the definitive collection of Google dorks — search queries that find misconfigured, exposed, or vulnerable systems and data using Google's index.
howTo: Browse by category: Files containing passwords, Sensitive Directories, Error Messages, etc.
Click a dork to view the query
proTip: Always get written permission before using dorks against a specific target's infrastructure. For your own investigation …

name: Google Dork Cheatsheet
summary: Reference for all Google search operators with examples.
detail: Comprehensive cheatsheet for Google's advanced search operators: site:, filetype:, inurl:, intitle:, cache:, link:, before:, after:, and combinations. Essential reference for building effective dork q…
howTo: Bookmark for reference during investigations
Combine operators for targeted searches: site:target.com filetype:pdf intext:password

name: Pagodo
summary: Automates Google dork searches from the GHDB against a target.
detail: Python tool that automatically runs GHDB dorks against a target domain using Google search. Finds exposed files, login pages, error messages, and other sensitive information.
howTo: Clone: git clone https://github.com/opsdisk/pagodo.git
Install: pip install -r requirements.txt
installCommand: git clone https://github.com/opsdisk/pagodo && pip install -r pagodo/requirements.txt

name: Public AWS S3 & Azure Search
summary: Search for publicly exposed cloud storage buckets.
detail: Searches for files inside publicly exposed Amazon S3 buckets and Azure Blob Storage containers. Massive amounts of sensitive data are accidentally left public in cloud storage.
howTo: Enter keywords (company name, domain, product name)
Review files found in public cloud buckets
proTip: Search for the target's domain name, product names, and employee names — companies often name their buckets after their …

name: FilePhish
summary: Builds filetype-specific Google dork queries for finding documents.
detail: GUI tool that generates Google dork queries for finding specific file types on a target domain. Select the domain and file type (PDF, XLS, DOC, etc.) and it builds the query for you.
howTo: Enter the target domain
Select one or more file types to search for

name: Open Directory Finder
summary: Searches Google for open directory listings.
detail: Generates Google dork queries specifically for finding web servers with open directory listings (Apache/Nginx index pages). These often contain files the owner didn't intend to expose.
howTo: Enter the target domain or keyword
Run the generated Google query

name: FilePursuit
summary: Search engine for files on public FTP and web servers.
detail: Indexes files from public FTP servers, HTTP open directories, and cloud storage. Search by filename, extension, or keyword. Find documents, media, and software exposed on public servers.
howTo: Enter a filename, extension, or keyword
Filter by file type using the type selector

name: Mamont's FTP Index
summary: Index of files on public FTP servers worldwide.
detail: Indexes millions of files on publicly accessible FTP servers. Search by filename. Surprisingly often contains corporate documents, database backups, and media that were accidentally left on public FTP…
howTo: Enter a filename or keyword
Browse results from public FTP servers

name: Google Dataset Search
summary: Google's search engine specifically for finding datasets.
detail: Searches thousands of dataset repositories, government portals, and academic data sources. Find datasets by topic, format, license, and update frequency.
howTo: Enter your topic
Filter by format (CSV, JSON, etc.) and license

name: Data.gov
summary: US Federal Government open data portal — 300,000+ datasets.
detail: The US government's open data portal. 300,000+ datasets covering agriculture, climate, education, energy, finance, health, public safety, and more. All data is in the public domain.
howTo: Search by topic or agency
Filter by format, frequency, and publisher

name: OpenSanctions
summary: Open database of sanctioned entities from 60+ countries plus PEP data.
detail: Aggregates sanctions lists from the US (OFAC), EU, UN, UK, and 60+ other jurisdictions, plus Politically Exposed Person (PEP) data. Downloadable in bulk and searchable via API.
howTo: Search by name for instant results
Download the full dataset for bulk screening: available in CSV, JSON, and Excel

name: Kaggle
summary: Largest community platform for datasets and data science notebooks.
detail: Hosts 50,000+ public datasets across all topics. Many OSINT-relevant datasets exist: social media data, breach data, geolocation data, and more. Also has Jupyter notebook examples for analysis.
howTo: Search for your topic
Filter by dataset type and size

name: GitHub Code Search
summary: Search all public GitHub repos for code, files, and commits.
detail: GitHub's powerful code search. Search across billions of files in public repositories. Find API keys, credentials, internal hostnames, and other sensitive data accidentally committed to public repos.
howTo: Use the Code search tab
Search: org:targetcompany password or org:targetcompany apikey
proTip: Use: path:.env to find .env files. path:config OR path:settings combined with a company name often surfaces credentials.

name: Grep.app
summary: Fast regex search across 500,000 GitHub repositories.
detail: Faster and more regex-capable than GitHub's native search. Searches across 500,000 public repos. Use regular expressions to find patterns like API keys, connection strings, and email addresses in code…
howTo: Enter a keyword or regex pattern
Filter by language or repository
proTip: Combine with company name: search 'COMPANY_NAME' with regex for key patterns to find employee-committed secrets.
